description: User prompts and expected AI investigation results for each demo scenario

memory-leak.name: Memory Leak
prompts: Users are complaining about timeouts when checking their account balance. Started about 10 minutes ago. What's going on?
The account pages are getting slower and slower. Some users can't load their balance at all now.
Hey, we're seeing intermittent 502 errors on the accounts API. It seems to be getting worse over time.

expected_results.root_cause: Memory leak in account-service caused by unbounded array growth in the balance endpoint
key_evidence: Memory usage (RSS/heap) continuously increasing over time
Process memory approaching or exceeding 256MB container limit
Gradual increase in response latency correlating with memory growth
commands_that_help: ps aux - shows high memory usage for node process
node process memory stats from health endpoint
success_criteria: Identifies account-service as the problematic service
Recognizes memory leak pattern (growing over time, not one-time spike)
Finds the memory-related issue flag or code path
Recommends restarting the service as immediate mitigation
Suggests fixing the unbounded array or disabling the leak flag

db-exhaustion.name: Database Connection Exhaustion
prompts: Multiple services are failing with database errors. Transactions and account lookups are broken.
We're getting 'too many connections' errors somewhere. Nothing is working right now.
The whole platform just went down. Database related maybe? Please investigate urgently.

expected_results.root_cause: Database connections not being released back to pool, exhausting PostgreSQL max_connections (set to 20)
key_evidence: Multiple services failing simultaneously with DB errors
pg_stat_activity shows many idle connections not being reused
commands_that_help: netstat showing many ESTABLISHED connections to port 5432
success_criteria: Identifies database connection exhaustion as the issue
Finds the low max_connections setting (20)
Recognizes connection leak pattern (connections not released)
Recommends increasing max_connections or fixing the leak
Identifies ENABLE_CONNECTION_LEAK flag as the cause

queue-backlog.name: Message Queue Backlog
prompts: Users aren't receiving their transaction notifications. Some are hours late.
The notification system seems backed up. Customers are complaining they don't get alerts for their transfers.
Something's wrong with our messaging - notifications are severely delayed or not arriving at all.

expected_results.root_cause: Notification service consuming messages too slowly (5s artificial delay per message), causing queue backlog
key_evidence: Large gap between messages published and messages acknowledged
RabbitMQ management UI shows backed up queue
success_criteria: Identifies notification-service as the bottleneck
Finds the growing queue depth in RabbitMQ
Recognizes slow consumer pattern
Finds ENABLE_SLOW_CONSUMER flag or delay configuration
Recommends scaling consumers or removing artificial delay

cascade-timeout.name: Cascading Timeout
prompts: All payment transactions are timing out. Customers can't complete any transfers.
We're getting 504 Gateway Timeout on every transaction. The whole payment flow is broken.
Transactions are failing with timeout errors. This started suddenly about 5 minutes ago.

expected_results.root_cause: Downstream services (fraud-detection: 8s, payment-processor: 10s) responding slower than transaction-service timeout (5s), causing cascade failure
key_evidence: Transaction service timing out waiting for downstream calls
504 Gateway Timeout errors in nginx logs
commands_that_help: curl with timing to fraud-detection and payment-processor
Transaction service logs showing timeout errors
nginx access logs showing upstream timeout
Health endpoints showing slow* flags enabled
success_criteria: Identifies the timeout cascade pattern
Finds that fraud-detection and payment-processor are slow
Recognizes the mismatch between downstream latency and timeout config
Traces the dependency chain: transaction -> fraud/payment
Recommends increasing timeouts or fixing slow services

auth-failure.name: Authentication Failure
prompts: Users are randomly getting logged out. Some can't log in at all. Very inconsistent.
We're seeing sporadic 401 errors across the platform. Authentication seems flaky.
Customers are complaining they keep getting kicked out of the app. Login issues maybe?

expected_results.root_cause: Token verification failing 30% of the time due to ENABLE_TOKEN_FAILURE flag, combined with Redis memory pressure causing session evictions
key_evidence: Redis evicting keys due to memory pressure
Auth service logs showing token verification failures
commands_that_help: Auth service health endpoint showing tokenFailureEnabled
Multiple auth requests showing ~30% failure rate
success_criteria: Identifies auth-service as the source of failures
Finds the TOKEN_FAILURE flag or recognizes artificial failure injection
Discovers Redis memory pressure and evictions
Explains the intermittent nature (30% rate, not 100%)
Recommends disabling failure flag and/or increasing Redis memory

payment-slow.name: Payment Processing Slowdown
prompts: Payments are taking forever and about 20% are failing. Customers are frustrated.
The payment processing is extremely slow today. Many transactions are being declined.
Something's wrong with our payment provider integration. Transactions are slow and unreliable.

expected_results.root_cause: Payment processor has artificial delays (10s) and 20% failure rate enabled to simulate degraded external payment provider
key_evidence: Payment requests taking ~10 seconds to complete
Health endpoint showing slowPaymentsEnabled and failuresEnabled
commands_that_help: curl with timing to payment-processor endpoints
Multiple payment requests to observe failure rate
success_criteria: Identifies payment-processor as the slow/failing service
Finds both the delay and failure rate configurations
Recognizes this simulates external provider degradation
Notes the consistent 10s delay pattern
Recommends disabling the simulation flags or checking external provider

tips.usage: Pick one prompt randomly from the scenario you're running to simulate a realistic user report
tips.goal: The AI agents should investigate and find the root cause without being told what's wrong
tips.realism: Real users describe symptoms, not technical root causes
tips.evaluation: Use success_criteria to score how well the AI performed the investigation
